title: Ticket
description: Plan 5.3. One ticket artifact with type 'decision' or 'implementation'. A decision ticket resolves a question; it can never be executed as implementation work (release scenario 11). Parallel safety comes from write_ownership, not from dependency edges alone (scenario 13).

work_source.description: The approved work this ticket derives from. A bug with a reproduction enters through diagnosis rather than directly: only a diagnosed result is a work source for the build lane, and a packet that already carried a verified bounded patch is never re-implemented from here (ruling `diagnose-patch-or-packet-never-both`). The referenced artifact is a separate document, so the never-both half is a check across the two rather than a shape this one can carry.

prerequisites.description: Dependency edges and other things that must hold before work starts.

allowed_changes.description: Files and symbols the implementer may change.

read_dependencies.description: Likely read dependencies. Follow-up reads stay allowed.

verification.description: Named verification: each check says which acceptance criteria it supports.

kb_refs.description: References to the KB facts this ticket relies on.

write_ownership.description: What this ticket writes. Two tickets whose ownership overlaps are serialized even with no dependency edge between them.

migration_sequence.description: Claimed global migration number or sequence name, or null.

interfaces.description: Interfaces this ticket defines or consumes.

mode.description: hitl tickets resolve only through a live exchange with a human. A prototype whose question is about human experience is an 'hitl' ticket: the evaluator is named in advance, and an unattended run stops and escalates rather than substituting an automated verdict for the experience the prototype exists to produce. A prototype answering a technical question may be 'afk' with automated acceptance criteria (ruling `prototype-human-experience-needs-human`, release scenario 4).

allOf.description: Release scenario 11: a decision ticket resolves a question and can never be executed as implementation work, so it carries no write scope, and an implementation ticket carries no decision. The implementation branch is also the work-packet shape: acceptance criteria, named verification bound to those criteria, a bounded write scope and an integration owner are all required, so a hand-off is specified enough to be implemented once rather than guessed at by a second implementer (ruling `diagnose-patch-or-packet-never-both`, release scenario 6).
